plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like goblet-shaped flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The foliage emerges the following spring, then dies back before the next flowering. All parts are highly toxic due to colchicine.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in meadows and gardens across temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true crocus; it is in the family Colchicaceae. Colchicine from this plant is used in medicine to treat gout and is also used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall herbaceous perennial forming dense plumes of tiny golden-yellow flower heads on arching stems. It is a vital late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other pollinators preparing for autumn and winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to fall (August to October)
plants.location: North America, in meadows, roadsides and prairies; introduced and widespread in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often wrongly blamed for hay fever; its pollen is heavy and sticky and insect-carried, while the real culprit is usually ragweed blooming at the same time.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub with huge, artichoke-like flower heads surrounded by showy pink bracts, the largest of any protea. It is adapted to nutrient-poor, fire-prone fynbos soils and is a symbol of South Africa.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (August to November, peaking around September)
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa (fynbos)
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its genus is named after Proteus, the shape-shifting Greek god, because of the great diversity of forms in the family.

plants.name: Cyclamen hederifolium
plants.description: A low-growing tuberous perennial with swept-back pink flowers that appear in early autumn before the marbled, ivy-shaped leaves unfurl. It thrives in woodland shade and can form large colonies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to November)
plants.location: Southern Europe and Western Asia; widely naturalized in gardens in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: After pollination, the flower stalks coil like springs and pull the seed capsules to the ground, where ants disperse the sticky seeds. Tubers can live for over 100 years.
